reports.text:
It was a slightly down week for the US stock market: the S&P 500 fund (Buy & Hold SPY) lost 0.37%. The news-reading agents point to oil above $110, a Federal Reserve (the US central bank) leaning toward higher interest rates, and a selloff in AI-linked shares.

The best of the main agents was Volatility Protected, up 1.57% for the week and 2.32% since the start. Over the same days SPY is down 3.0%. It made no trades all week and stayed fully invested, and its holdings Swiss SOON.SW (+6.4%) and XOM (+4.5%) did well. The worst was Bargain Hunter, down 1.75% this week. It made 12 trades, cashing in five small gains (about 2,000 CHF in total) and buying seven "cheap-looking" shares. Even so, it is up 0.36% since the start against SPY's -3.0%. Trend Follower slipped 0.39%, partly because it sold CSCO at a 914 CHF loss when its trend signal turned. It is still ahead of SPY (-2.45% vs -3.0%). The "(fixed)" twins show exactly the same numbers as the originals.

Some other things stood out. The Monkey, which picks at random, gained 1.0% this week and 1.72% since joining, while SPY lost 3.46% over those days. Luck can look a lot like skill. The two News Analysts agree on the big picture, favouring energy and defensive companies over tech. Over its own days the Sonnet-based one is up 1.07% and the Opus twin 0.18%, but the Opus twin joined a week later, so that is not a fair race. Opus Learner approved two buys on Monday (KO and XLV), but its latest status says Opus approved none of 12 picks. The Team Manager made 18 trades but still backs all agents equally until it has 35 days of results (10 so far). The new Buy & Hold All Markets account started only on October 22, so there is nothing to compare yet.

One week is far too short to judge skill, so treat all of this as noise.

The lesson: being busy isn't the same as being better. The agent that did nothing led the pack, and the one trading most finished last this week, so every trade needs a good reason.

The week of 12 to 16 October was rough for the broad market: Buy & Hold SPY fell 2.7%. Tech and AI stocks sold off while oil climbed to around $110 and inflation came in hot, so money moved into energy, healthcare and everyday-goods companies.

The best agent was the Bargain Hunter, up 2.2%. It buys shares that have dropped a lot and look due for a bounce. It bought Verizon, AT&T and Deutsche Telekom on Monday, and Verizon was up 5.5% by Friday. The worst was the Trend Follower, down 2.25%. It still edged out SPY, but it held Brazil's EWZ fund (down 4.1%) and Microsoft (down 1.3%). Its "fixed" twin, like the other fixed twins, had identical numbers.

Several agents beat the Monkey (random picks), which made 0.7%. The AI Learner made 1.05%, and the Volatility Protected agent made 0.73%, level with the Monkey. The AI Learner also sold ABBV at random just to learn from it, which happened to earn 289 CHF.

The News Analyst, running on Claude Sonnet, gained 0.5%. Its twin on the stronger Opus model lost 0.3%. Sonnet bought on Monday and held energy stocks like Chevron and Exxon, which rose about 5%. Opus only started buying on Thursday and owned an energy fund that slipped slightly. The Opus Learner approved just 2 of 12 picks, kept 40% in cash and ended flat. The Team Manager is still spreading money equally, since it needs 35 days of results and has only 4. It was down 0.4% with about half its money in cash and 19 orders waiting.

One week is far too short to judge skill, so none of this proves anything.

The lesson is that being spread across different kinds of investments, with some cash on the side, softened a bad week. The SPY fund held only one thing, an index dominated by the tech giants that sold off, and it lost more than almost every agent. Holding different kinds of investments usually means a smoother ride, though not always a higher return.
